sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Constitutional Basis under Article 270**: Taxes levied and collected by the Union are shared between the Centre and the States, but **surcharges** and **cesses** levied for specific purposes under **Article 271** are excluded from the divisible pool.
• **Non-Sharable Divisible Pool**: Surcharges and cesses remain exclusively with the Central Government, bypassing the Finance Commission's devolution recommendations.
• **Tax on Tax Nature**: Surcharges are calculated as a percentage of the base tax liability, whereas cesses can be levied as a percentage of tax or as a specific duty on goods/services.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Over the last decade, the share of cesses and surcharges in Gross Tax Revenue (GTR) has risen significantly from around 10% to over 20%, impacting state fiscal autonomy.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Levied on income tax and corporate tax when taxable income exceeds specified slabs (e.g., 50 lakh, 1 crore, 5 crore).
Exclusive revenue of the Centre; not shareable with states under Article 270/271.
Directly impacts cooperative federalism debates in GS Mains.

Governed by the Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2017.
Important for federal fiscal disputes and GST council dynamics.

items.definition: All taxes collected by the Union government, excluding central GST, cesses, and surcharges levied for specific purposes, which are shared with states according to Finance Commission formulas.
Empowers Parliament to increase any of the duties or taxes referred to in Articles 269 and 270 by way of a surcharge for Union purposes, excluding them from the divisible pool without state sharing.
Funds like Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Nidhi (PMSSN) or Madhyamik and Uchchatar Shiksha Kosh (MUSK) where cess collections are pooled to ensure non-lapsable funding for specific welfare schemes.
Noted the disproportionate rise in cesses and surcharges and recommended that the Central government should streamline non-shareable revenue instruments to strengthen state finances.

items.title: Impact on Fiscal Federalism & State Finances
items.content:
• **Revenue Erosion for States**: Expansion of cesses and surcharges shrinks the size of the divisible tax pool, reducing statutory resource transfers to states.
• **Conditional vs. Unconditional Transfers**: States prefer unconditional devolution via Finance Commission recommendations over tied-fund cesses managed centrally.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Lack of transparency in the utilization of specific cesses, accumulation of unspent balances in dedicated funds.
• **Policy Interventions**: Institutionalizing a cap on cesses and surcharges as a percentage of gross tax revenue; greater transparency mandated by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG).

items.title: Mnemonic for Constitutional Articles
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: **S**hare **P**ool **C**entre (SPC)
• **Decoded Meaning**: **S**urcharges (Article **271**), **P**ool = Divisible **P**ool (Article **270**), **C**entre keeps them exclusively.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly recalls that surcharges are kept by the Centre and excluded from state sharing.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember **'Cess = Cause'** (Cess is always tied to a specific purpose/cause like education or health) and **'Surcharge = Size'** (Surcharge depends on the size of income).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often frames statements like 'Proceeds from all cesses and surcharges are mandatorily shared with states based on Finance Commission devolution.' This is completely incorrect; cesses and surcharges are part of the Consolidated Fund of India but are NOT part of the divisible pool shared with states.

Mains Value Addition: Quote the 15th Finance Commission report observations on 'vertical imbalance' caused by the rising trend of cesses and surcharges (which grew from around 10.4% of Gross Tax Revenue in 2011-12 to over 20% in recent years) to score exceptional marks in questions concerning fiscal federalism.

keyTakeaways: Surcharges are additional taxes on tax liability dependent on income slabs, while cesses are earmarked taxes for specific welfare purposes.
Both instruments bypass the divisible pool of taxes under Article 270, meaning revenues are retained entirely by the Central Government.
The unabated rise of cesses and surcharges poses a structural challenge to Indian fiscal federalism by shrinking state shares in central taxes.
